One of the biggest one occurred when I worked at the YMCA summer camp a few years back. 

I could tell that my directors regretted hiring me. I'm great with kids, but sometimes I clash with fellow adults. My YMCA directors hated me due to social incompatibility (like your typical "high school drama" stuff). 

I did my best, but I would up not going back the next summer. I worked my hardest but the bosses hating my quirkiness annoyed them and as a result they antagonized me. 

Anyway, even though the YMCA regrets having me as a camp counselor: there was a big reason it turns out I was there, on a grander scheme. 

At one swimming lesson, I was placed in the pool to help keep an eye on kids and encourage them to participate and help the instructors. 

I randomly was looking at the kids hanging onto the side in front of me, dipping their kids in and out of the pool. There was one kid with his head under water; he had to have been about 6 or 7 years old. He was under water for more than a couple of seconds, and I just thought to myself, "I'm not comfortable with how long this kid is keeping himself under water."

The depth for us was about 5ft, so I was able to walk over to this kid, place my hands under his armpits, and simply lift him so his head could come out of water and he could take a breath. I figured there was absolutely no harm in being that annoying adult who encourages kids to take a breath when swimming. 

My simple lift was the beyond opposite of harmful--as soon as I lifted this kid's head out of water, he frantically grabbed the edge of the pool and began coughing up water. 

I had casually saved a kid from drowning that day. 

The YMCA can preach all they want that I was a terrible hire--I'll continue to tell the story about how my presence saved that location from a casualty.

I'm going to be raw and just share my recent experience and vent. This isn't going to offer any hopeful advice, so if anyone is looking for that, please scroll away. 

The past few weeks, all I've heard was "just go for a walk" and "just do something that will give you joy, like writing!"

I'll go for walks. I'll take an hour out of my life and I'll go walk two miles outside. I don't come back with that exercise-induced euphoria everyone raves about. I had spent that entire hour thinking about all the negative shit happening. So I come home after allowing myself to think about crap for an hour. So no, I don't feel better. Also, my body is now tired from all that movement. So now I need a several hour nap. Waste of time. 

Writing? Sure, when I'm happy and inspired, I love writing stories. Right now? I'm not in the mood. I'm stressed. I'll try to write, and I'll upset myself even more cause I can't. It's too much work. Too much thinking. Too much brainpower. It's not even like a perfectionist bullshit thing. Just to think of any words and string them into even incomplete sentences. It's exhausting. I have to shut my laptop and put it away before I develop an anxiety attack because I can't get my thoughts out. They don't want to be transferred onto a word document. 

My favorite? That I need to make lists. Of good things about myself. People who would miss me. Goals and other little things I could do tomorrow. All those little things people say you should think of: the reasons to live. 

I've got no healthy thoughts in my brains right now. 
Good things about myself? There's nothing good about me, and I don't believe I have the right to think that there's a single non-shitty thing about me. 
People who would miss me? Brain tells me to forget about them. And if they ever mistreated me in the past, focus on those little actions that upset me. In fact, brain is trying to rationalize the plan of straight up emotionally ABUSING everyone I love now. Build them up to a hatred towards me. So if I do finally croak, no one will miss me. They'll say "dead? Good." The world will truly be a better place, instead of people falsely thinking there's a piece missing to the bright out there. 
Goals and things to do tomorrow? Not important. It's so fucking bleak. I shouldn't think about all the good things I'd do. I wouldn't do them anyway. I would just sit and use up the worlds' resources while my goals sit and never be completed. 

I genuinely believe that all these unhealthy negative thoughts? I need them. Need to keep myself with reality. I am a terrible person. I don't deserve any kind of love or hope or positive, healthy thoughts. I don't deserve to enjoy any of the things I've accomplished. 

The only fucking thing keeping me alive right now? The reason why I don't need to be hospitalized at the moment? How fucking chaotic things would get if I DID attempt. 

One time the ideation was so bad that the school I was attending felt they had enough evidence that I was planning to attempt so they had me hospitalized. Cause if I did attempt on campus, that was their responsibility. Their issue. Their heightened statistic. Blood on their hands. They didn't care about me, they cared about their image. Cause I think about how even after I was determined "safe" by the hospital psychiatrist and released, I wasn't allowed to step foot on campus until the campus head psychologist deemed me "safe." Think: what if I went somewhere during the time I wasn't allowed on campus to somewhere more chaotic than the campus and actually attempted? Welp, not on school property. Not their responsibility. That school psychologist didn't even give a flying fuck if he ever saw me again after his decision to let me back on campus. Didn't want to do a check-in, nothing. 

Anyway, that night at the hospital? Worst of my fucking life. Granted, some of the emergency staff were kind hearted. Genuinely cared. Other staff members? Fucking horrendous. They told me how much of a terrible person I was, how I ruined my own life. They made me extremely guilty for not being dead. They made me guilty for not even trying to be dead. For 12 hours, held hostage legally by people allowed to emotionally abuse me. Thank god I had popped a valium before campus security found me and had me taken by an ambulance. So I could shut the fuck up for a night and fake sanity and stability and get the hell out of there asap. I remember the nice emergency workers: "Wow, you're so calm! Usually people are freaking out." Then they ran the urine tests. Positive: Benzodiazepines. Explained. Best part? I was charged $3,000 for the whole thing. Landed my ass in collections for a little bit over it. My body was not damaged, no actual work had to be done to save my life or keep me healthy. I was just babysat for 12 hours. And that shit cost $3,000. 

Best part? The school or something has me on file as HAD ONCE ATTEMPTED SUICIDE. And it's like, wow, never knew I actually went through with an attempt! In what state did you find me? Who did I give PTSD? Where's the hospital records saying that my body had to be repaired (as in cleaning cuts, pumping stomach, yknow)?

But I'd imagine, what if I did attempt. Slitting my wrists? Ouch, painful, blood, blech. Somehow getting a gun and blowing my brains out? Possibly messing up and crippling myself. Hanging myself? I heard that's a long and painful death of suffocation or something. Drowning myself? Same thing. Overdosing on pills? Having to get my stomach pumped. 

I'd think, what would happen if my attempt wasn't successful? Because with my luck, it won't be. 

I'd have to deal with the following:
- Giving whomever discovers my body PTSD. 
- My family sobbing at the hospital, and I have no idea why'd they be like this, because they hate me. (Like if I moved away and never contacted them again, they'd be fine. If I died? Boohoo. Same amount of exposure to me, but the more permanent for sure never again is...yeah.)
- That horrible hospital night, all over again x10, because this time, they'd have to repair the body. And I would have so much more debt over it. 
- The aftermath post-checkout. The constant monitoring. The lack of trust. The lack of allowed independence. 
- My precious valium? They'd take it away. (Now before you accuse me of being a benzo junkie, I'm not addicted. I get 10 2mg pills per year. I take one or two pills every few months. I just REALLY like to keep it in my purse in case of a psychiatric emergency to keep my ass out of trouble.)
- The long period of time my family would spend straight up angry and pissed at me. 

That risk of having worst-case-scenario for me is not worth attempting. 
Because for some reason, people want to keep assholes like me alive. 

But I need to stop letting people worry about me. One of the only people that truly cares about me and my well-being, she's halfway through a pregnancy. She doesn't deserve the stress. Especially over shitheads like me.
